questions.title: Sum of Array Elements
questions.description:
Read a single line of space-separated integers and print their total sum.

Input Format:
One line containing N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single integer, the sum of the input integers.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= each value <= 10000.

questions.title: Library Book Inventory Total
questions.description:
A small library branch keeps the per-shelf book count in an array. Compute the total number of books across all shelves by iterating the array with an each loop. The sum, reduce and inject methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N (number of shelves).
Line 2: N space-separated integer counts.

Output Format:
A single integer: the total number of books.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= each count <= 10000.
questions.sourcecode:
def total_books(counts)
  total = 0
  counts.each { |c| total += c }
  total
end

n = gets.to_i

puts total_books(counts)

questions.title: Marathon Peak Distance Finder
questions.description:
A marathon organiser records the distance each runner covered in metres and wants the longest distance. Find the maximum value by iterating the array with each. The max, min and sort methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integer distances.

Output Format:
A single integer: the longest distance.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= each distance <= 100000.
questions.sourcecode:
def find_peak(distances)
  best = distances[0]
  distances.each { |d| best = d if d > best }
  best
end

n = gets.to_i
distances = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts find_peak(distances)

questions.title: Reverse Train Car Order
questions.description:
A yardmaster needs the train cars printed in reverse order without using the reverse method. Build the reversed list using a while loop. The reverse and sort methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integer car labels.

Output Format:
N space-separated integers in reverse order on one line.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= each label <= 100000.
questions.sourcecode:
def flip_cars(cars)
  result = []
  i = cars.length - 1
  while i >= 0
    result << cars[i]
    i -= 1
  end
  result
end

n = gets.to_i
cars = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts flip_cars(cars).join(" ")

questions.title: Bubble Scoreboard Ordering
questions.description:
A coach wants the scoreboard sorted in ascending order of scores. Implement bubble sort with a while loop. The sort, max and min methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integer scores.

Output Format:
N space-separated integers in ascending order on one line.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= each score <= 100.
questions.sourcecode:
def bubble_order(scores)
  arr = scores.dup
  n = arr.length
  swapped = true
  while swapped
    swapped = false
    (n - 1).times do |i|
      if arr[i] > arr[i + 1]
        arr[i], arr[i + 1] = arr[i + 1], arr[i]
        swapped = true
      end
    end
  end
  arr
end

n = gets.to_i
scores = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts bubble_order(scores).join(" ")

questions.title: Top K Marathon Finishers
questions.description:
Given marathon finish times for N runners, print the top K fastest finishers. Each output line is the runner's original bib number (1-indexed) followed by their time. Implement sorting with a while loop. The sort, max, min, sort_by and group_by methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integer finish times.
Line 3: integer K (1 <= K <= N).

Output Format:
K lines, each containing the bib number and time separated by a space, ordered by ascending time.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= K <= N, 1 <= each time <= 10^9.
questions.sourcecode:
def top_k_finishers(times, k)
  pairs = []
  times.each_with_index { |t, i| pairs << [t, i] }
  n = pairs.length
  swapped = true
  while swapped
    swapped = false
    (n - 1).times do |j|
      if pairs[j][0] > pairs[j + 1][0]
        pairs[j], pairs[j + 1] = pairs[j + 1], pairs[j]
        swapped = true
      end
    end
  end
  k.times do |i|
    t, idx = pairs[i]
    puts "#{idx + 1} #{t}"
  end
end

n = gets.to_i
times = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
k = gets.to_i
top_k_finishers(times, k)

questions.title: Stock Trading Profit Peaks
questions.description:
Given an array of stock prices on consecutive days, find the maximum profit achievable by buying once and selling once on a later day. If no profit is possible, output 0. Iterate the prices with each_with_index. The max, min, sort, reduce, inject and select methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integer prices.

Output Format:
A single integer: the maximum profit (0 if no profit is possible).

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= each price <= 10000.
questions.blacklist: max, min, sort, reduce, inject, select
questions.sourcecode:
def best_profit(prices)
  cheapest = prices[0]
  best = 0
  prices.each_with_index do |p, i|
    next if i == 0
    diff = p - cheapest
    best = diff if diff > best
    cheapest = p if p < cheapest
  end
  best
end

n = gets.to_i
prices = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts best_profit(prices)

questions.title: Subarray Sum Counter
questions.description:
Given an array of N integers and a threshold K, count the number of contiguous subarrays whose sum is less than or equal to K. Use nested iteration with each_with_index (outer) and a while loop (inner). The sum, reduce, inject, select and max methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integers.
Line 3: integer K.

Output Format:
A single integer: the count of subarrays whose sum is <= K.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, -1000 <= each value <= 1000, -10^6 <= K <= 10^6.
questions.sourcecode:
def count_subarrays(arr, k)
  n = arr.length
  count = 0
  arr.each_with_index do |_, i|
    running = 0
    j = i
    while j < n
      running += arr[j]
      count += 1 if running <= k
      j += 1
    end
  end
  count
end

n = gets.to_i
arr = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
k = gets.to_i
puts count_subarrays(arr, k)

questions.title: Rainwater Harvest Trap
questions.description:
An array of non-negative integers represents the elevation map of a rainwater harvesting trench of width N. Compute how many units of water can be trapped after raining using the two-pointer technique with a while loop. The max, min, sort, reduce and select methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated non-negative integers (heights).

Output Format:
A single integer: total units of trapped water.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= each height <= 10000.
questions.sourcecode:
def trap_water(heights)
  left = 0
  right = heights.length - 1
  left_bound = 0
  right_bound = 0
  total = 0
  while left <= right
    if heights[left] <= heights[right]
      if heights[left] >= left_bound
        left_bound = heights[left]
      else
        total += left_bound - heights[left]
      end
      left += 1
    else
      if heights[right] >= right_bound
        right_bound = heights[right]
      else
        total += right_bound - heights[right]
      end
      right -= 1
    end
  end
  total
end

n = gets.to_i
heights = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts trap_water(heights)
